=== PUC Project No. 58481_Interconnection Agreement Standards.pdf ===
                                               PUC PROJECT NO. 58481


                                                       §
    INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS                          §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
                                                       §
             FOR LARGE LOADS                           §                    OF TEXAS
                                                       §
                                                       §

                                              I.​   INTRODUCTION


        Schaper Energy Consulting LLC (“Respondent”) advises data center developers participating in

the ERCOT large load interconnection process, including clients representing a meaningful share of the

most advanced large load projects currently proceeding in Texas. Respondent submits these comments to

assist Commission Staff in refining the proposed large load interconnection standards and to address

issues that have become increasingly concrete in related ERCOT implementation proceedings.

Respondent has made parallel comments on this same topic in ERCOT’s PGRR145 proceeding and offers

these comments here so that Staff may address the issue in this rulemaking rather than leaving it to later

interpretation in collateral proceedings.


                       II.​   INTERCONNECTION AGREEMENT STANDARDS


        Respondent appreciates the Commission Staff’s work in Project No. 58481 and supports the

Commission’s effort to establish a clear and workable framework for large load interconnections going

forward. Respondent is concerned, however, that absent clearer applicability provisions, the Proposal for

Publication could be read or later implemented in a manner that extends the new framework to projects

that already advanced under the existing ERCOT rules, completed the legacy study process, and executed

binding interconnection agreements in reliance on the standards that governed at the time. Respondent

submits these comments to elaborate on this concern in the hope that Staff can address it directly in the

applicability provisions of the final rule.

                                                                                                        1
         Our concern stems from the original PGRR145 (“Batch Zero Process for Large Load

Interconnections”) draft published on March 4, 2026, and ERCOT’s subsequent revisions filed on March

17, 2026, which seek to conform the Intermediate and Interconnection Agreement standards under

proposed ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 9.7.1 and 9.7.2 to the proposal for publication in this docket. Under

that revised draft, projects seeking Batch Zero treatment as ‘Base Load Not Subject to Additional Study in

Batch Zero’ under proposed ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1 must hold an executed interconnection

agreement meeting revised proposed ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.7.2, and modeled load levels are tied to

the peak Demand stated in a conforming agreement. With that proposed implementation, the practical

effect is that agreements executed and funded under the legacy framework risk being treated as

insufficient unless they are re-papered to conform to a new agreement model derived from this

rulemaking.


        We view 16 TAC §25.194 to be structured as a prospective framework for new large load

interconnection requests. It contemplates an intermediate agreement executed before study initiation,

culminating in a post-study interconnection agreement that introduces new commercial obligations,

including a non-refundable interconnection fee, CIAC for direct interconnection costs, and financial

security for both significant equipment and system upgrades. That structure may be workable for projects

entering under a new regulatory regime. It is not, however, readily administrable for projects that have

already completed the study phase, executed interconnection arrangements, and incurred material

financial obligations in reliance on the existing Planning Guide framework, for the reasons of implied

retroactivity and inadministrability described herein.


        Absent an express ‘prospective-only’ applicability provision, the final rule risks supplanting the

operative interconnection agreement framework for in-flight projects after the fact. These projects were

not pursued speculatively — they were advanced in good-faith reliance on the existing Planning Guide

framework. Load customers completed the full study process, executed binding utility agreements, and


                                                                                                        2
 committed capital accordingly. By this stage, it is not uncommon for a large load customer to have placed

tens of millions of dollars at risk through security deposits and CIAC obligations for the interconnection

facilities required to serve its load.


        Imposing revised agreement requirements on those projects retroactively is particularly

unworkable given the compressed timeline ERCOT has outlined for Batch Zero implementation. Under

ERCOT’s published notional timeline, PGRR145 would not receive ERCOT board approval until at least

June 1, 2026, with a notional effective date of August 1, 2026 for the Planning Guide revision request, yet

projects must meet the promulgated interconnection agreement standards by July 10, 2026 under current

draft PGRR145 language. That sequence affords no practical opportunity for utilities and large load

customers to determine whether their existing agreements satisfy a revised — and still-evolving —

standard; negotiate the necessary amendments across what may be multiple interconnection and facilities

extension agreements with transmission and distribution utilities; arrange any newly required financial

security; and complete the attestations necessary to preserve their projects’ status as a ‘Base Load Not

Subject to Additional Study in Batch Zero’ under PGRR145.


        Respondent has proposed language in the PGRR145 proceeding that would deem projects

satisfying the existing ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.5 interconnection agreement standards before the July

10, 2026 compliance deadline as compliant with any revised interconnection agreement requirements,

provided those projects are otherwise eligible for inclusion in Batch Zero as Loads Not Subject to

Additional Study under proposed ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1. That approach would alleviate this

issue and prevent disruption to legacy projects.


        Respondent respectfully submits that, while it intends to address this issue in ERCOT's PGRR145

proceedings as well, it is important that Staff resolve the matter directly in the applicability provisions of

the final rule. Specifically, the final rule should make clear that 16 TAC §25.194 applies prospectively to

new interconnection requests and does not require projects that have already completed the ERCOT study

                                                                                                            3
 process and executed binding interconnection agreements under the prior framework to conform existing

agreements to standards derived from this rulemaking, execute new agreements incorporating

§25.194-type terms, or risk loss of project status because their legacy arrangements do not conform to a

subsequently adopted template. Respondent intends to file redlines proposing specific applicability

language within the current proposal for publication, but submits these comments at this time for Staff's

advance consideration.


                                            III.​   CLOSING


        Respondent appreciates the Staff’s considerable work on this rulemaking and acknowledges the

substantial effort reflected in the Proposal for Publication. The concerns raised herein are narrow in

scope: they seek only to ensure that the final rule operates prospectively and does not inadvertently

impose retroactive obligations on projects that proceeded in compliance with the standards in effect at the

time. Retroactive application of revised standards to these projects would risk significantly disrupting

investment activity and business development in Texas without meaningfully advancing the rule’s

objective of protecting against stranded costs, as load customers who completed the prior study process

and executed binding agreements have already necessarily provided security for the interconnection

facilities necessary to serve their loads. Respondent respectfully requests that Staff include an express

applicability provision in the final rule exempting projects that completed the ERCOT Planning Guide

§§9.4 and 9.5 study process and executed binding interconnection agreements prior to the rule’s effective

date from any requirement to conform existing agreements to standards derived from this rulemaking —

and that Staff ensure this treatment is carried through consistently in ERCOT’s parallel effort to embed

the rulemaking into PGRR145, so that projects are not subjected through implementation what the rule

itself does not require.




                                                                                                         4
 Respectfully submitted,




​
Schaper Energy Consulting, LLC
3006 Brazos St., Ste. 200
Houston, Texas 77006
andrew@schaperintl.com
